lead.zh-Hans: 绿灯罩下面，我把感叹号写小了。
lead.en: Under a green lamp shade, my exclamation mark shrank.

text.zh-Hans: 坐在墨尔本拉筹伯阅览室，我抬头看穹顶，又低头看放射排列的桌子。给你的信写了一个大大的“哇”，忽然觉得纸上也该安静一点。我没出声，只把感叹号改小，旁边留了一圈空白。离馆后再跟你讲它有多高。
text.en: At Melbourne’s La Trobe Reading Room, I looked from the dome to the radiating desks. My letter began with a huge written “wow.” Without making a sound, I reduced the exclamation mark and left some space around it. The tall-room conversation can wait until we are outside.
Describe the dome after leaving
Leave space for the small exclamation

lead.zh-Hans: 小径没有催我，鞋带倒催了。
lead.en: The path was patient. My shoelace was less so.

text.zh-Hans: 卡尔顿花园的林荫小径让我放慢脚步，鞋带偏在这时松开。系好抬头，皇家展览馆仍在，我却差点把“慢一点”写成“站一会儿”。两种都做到了。我在纸上画个小结，提醒回家收信的你，我一路有好好照看自己。
text.en: A tree-lined path in Carlton Gardens slowed me down, then a loose lace brought me to a halt. When I looked up, the Royal Exhibition Building was still there. “Take it slowly” had become “stand still.” I drew a small knot on the page to assure home that I am looking after myself.
Tell the reason for stopping
Look at the little drawn knot

lead.zh-Hans: 今天拆开的小包，不装信。
lead.en: Today’s little parcel contained no letters.

text.zh-Hans: 午饭选了蒸的 dim sim。我在墨尔本的小菜单上先写“咸味小包”，吃到肉馅才把菜名补完整。邮包待在椅边，没有申请分一口。我给它画在菜单角落，算它陪我按时吃了饭。
text.en: I chose a steamed dim sim in Melbourne. “Savoury parcel” went on the menu first; after reaching the meat filling, I added its name. My mailbag waited beside the chair without asking for a share. It got a corner of the drawing for keeping me company at lunch.
Introduce today’s little parcel
Finish writing the dish’s name

lead.zh-Hans: 第一眼没看见的，在点心里面。
lead.en: What I could not see was inside the doughnut.

text.zh-Hans: 维多利亚女王市场的果酱甜甜圈，外面的糖我一眼就看见了，果酱得咬开才知道。我想给你画一张诚实的菜单，便把里面也画出来。结果点心像开了小窗。窗里没有信使，信使正忙着把这一口吃好。
text.en: At Queen Victoria Market, the sugar on my jam doughnut was easy to see. The filling needed a bite. For an honest menu drawing, I included the inside too. The doughnut looked as though it had acquired a window. No messenger at that window: I was occupied with the rest of the snack.
Talk about the snack’s little window
Find sugar and jam in the drawing

lead.zh-Hans: 我把“还吃了什么”讲成了接力。
lead.en: “What else did you eat?” became a relay.

text.zh-Hans: 旅人问起墨尔本这顿饭，我说完 dim sim，才想起还有果酱甜甜圈。对方替我等了一下，让第二样赶上。我把两张菜单排好，终于没让点心在话尾落单。寄给你时，也留个空格，等你的晚饭来接下一棒。
text.en: A traveler asked about my Melbourne meal. I mentioned the dim sim, then remembered the jam doughnut. They waited for the second dish to catch up. Both menus now fit into the account. I left a gap for your supper to take the next turn when the letter gets home.
Let supper take the next turn
Look between the menus

lead.zh-Hans: 铅笔躺下，午饭才算画完。
lead.en: The pencil lay down when lunch was finally drawn.

text.zh-Hans: 吃过 dim sim 和果酱甜甜圈，我把墨尔本的两张菜单摊开，一张字挤，一张图大。只改了标题的位置，就都看得清了。我本来还想添花边，想起信还没写，便让铅笔休息。菜单少一圈装饰，你会多收到几句话。
text.en: After a dim sim and a jam doughnut, my Melbourne menus needed balancing: crowded words on one, an oversized sketch on the other. Moving the headings helped. I considered decorative borders, then remembered this letter. The pencil got a rest from ornament so I could send you a few more words.
Read the words that took their place
Compare the headings’ positions

lead.en: I made room for your words: “{reply}.”

text.zh-Hans: 你让小感叹号旁边留些空白，我把拉筹伯阅览室那页重新誊在一张折卡上。穹顶只画轮廓，绿灯罩占一个小角。那声没说出口的“哇”留在中间，轻轻的。纸折起来也没有挤到它，我试过了。
text.en: You suggested leaving space around the little exclamation. I copied the La Trobe Reading Room page onto a folded card: a dome outline, a green lamp shade in one corner. The silent “wow” has the middle to itself. Even folding the paper does not crowd it. I checked.
Read the silent exclamation
Notice the space after folding

lead.zh-Hans: 一只布球，把我留在了花园里。
lead.en: A cloth ball kept me in the gardens a little longer.

text.zh-Hans: 脚边滚来一只布球，我赶紧伸手拦住。皇家展览馆的轮廓还认得，这回进墨尔本的卡尔顿花园，却先被球领着离开了林荫小径。追来的孩子接过去，刚道谢又松了手，球沿草地滚回我身边。我索性在草地上蹲下来托住它，等他把外套穿好。临走，他把帽子翻了个面，布球正好窝在里面。
text.en: A cloth ball rolled against my foot, and I caught it before it went any farther. I still recognised the Royal Exhibition Building on this return to Melbourne, but something much smaller had drawn me off a tree-lined path in Carlton Gardens. The child chasing it said thank you, then let go to put on his coat. Back it came. I crouched and held it until both sleeves were sorted. Before leaving, he turned his hat upside down and tucked the ball inside.

text.zh-Hans: 给小球找个不乱跑的位置
text.en: Suggest somewhere the ball can stay put

text.zh-Hans: 看看帽子里窝着的布球
text.en: Look at the cloth ball tucked into the hat
